Harbor Rush · Metagame proposal

The Mega Storm

A cooperative territory SLG that resets the world every month.

Opening: Harbor Rush gets a full SLG layer, in the spirit of Last War, built around one story beat: a Mega Storm that wipes the world map every month. This deck is the high-level idea for discussion, not a locked spec. Items marked “proposal” or “TBD” are open.

The idea in one line

Every month a Mega Storm wipes the world. Four factions race to claim it before it returns.

Full SLG

Like Last War. Replaces Territory.

Cooperative

Team up with whoever you’re stranded with.

Monthly reset

New world. Account power carries over.

Harbor Rush · The Mega Storm · 2 · Concept art, AI-generated

The storm is the fiction that makes a monthly map reset feel natural, the same structure as Rust wipes or Diablo seasons. Long-term progression (tech, characters, cards, ship) is permanent. The world map, island ownership and faction score reset. The background is AI-generated concept art for mood only, not final art.

The storm resets the world

Harbor Rush · The Mega Storm · 3

The player journey through one month. 1) Find your faction: you wash up near a stronghold, join the faction that takes you in, and team up with new allies; old grudges don’t survive the storm. 2) Explore: sail out into the fog to discover new islands. 3) Compete: fight other factions for territory to become the strongest faction. 4) Scramble: as the storm nears, race to gather supplies and rewards. 5) Blown away: the Mega Storm hits, reshapes the world and scatters everyone, and the journey starts again in a new setup.

Who you play with · 1

Four factions on a globe

Assigned, not chosen

Equal distance, no corners

Strongholds never storm

Yellow centre, Red top, Blue right, Green left. Names are placeholders.

Harbor Rush · The Mega Storm · 4

Every player is assigned to one of four factions. Four points equally spaced on a sphere are the corners of a tetrahedron: each faction borders the other three at the same distance, so the map has no edges or corners to exploit. Each stronghold is calm and untouched by the storm.

Who you play with · 2

Your alliance travels with you

Alliance

Blown together

Faction

Harbor Rush · The Mega Storm · 5

Alliances of up to 30 are player-made and always blown to the same faction together. They exist for retention: the lasting friendships. Factions of about 2,500 are assigned by the game each storm and balanced using alliance and player power. The gold ring marks your alliance inside the faction.

Mega Storm

Harbor Rush · The Mega Storm · 6

This is what one faction sees from its own stronghold; all four factions grow out the same way at once. Week 1, the Reefs: protected waters for shelter, discovery and digging, with no captures. Week 2: Uncharted Waters open, and territory there can be contested. Week 3: calm water from different factions starts to meet, and players run into other factions. Week 4: the fight for control, with the biggest bosses and the riskiest islands. Day 30: the Mega Storm returns and the world resets.

The month · daily

The storm pulls back faster each day

New water opened per day

Day 1 · 1×

Day 10 · 19×

Harbor Rush · The Mega Storm · 7

Calm water spreads out from each stronghold. Every day the storm’s edge moves back by the same distance. Because the calm area is a circle, day n opens (2n − 1) times the water of day 1: day 10 opens 19 times as much. Discovery spreads across the whole month, and late joiners always find new water.

Harbor Rush · The Mega Storm · 8 · Map size > all players’ monthly stamina, so no one charts it all

Stamina burned equals distance sailed. Everyone gets the same daily stamina; speed-ups change when you arrive, not what the trip costs, so spending wins races to islands, attacks and defences, not more map. Sizing rule: sea area greater than players × daily stamina × 30 days ÷ stamina per sea-mile. Trips take 5 minutes to 24 hours and continue offline on a pinned heading. Finding an island auto-docks the ship and sends a notification. After a discovery the ship can’t leave for 10 minutes. Stamina recovers faster while docked.

The month · discovery

Chart the fog, find your first island

Peeks through

A sense of direction

Hidden

Found only up close

First landing

Bonus + name stamp

10-min camp

Scout, set up base

Harbor Rush · The Mega Storm · 9

Players sail out from the stronghold into the fog of war. Some islands peek through the fog as faint shapes, giving players a sense of direction to sail toward. Others are completely hidden and only found by sailing close; the dashed circle is the ship’s sight radius. Finding an island auto-docks the ship and stops the journey. The first discoverer gets a one-time bonus and their name stamped on the island; stamps reset with every storm because every island is new. After a discovery the ship can’t leave for 10 minutes, the in-fiction time to scout and set up a small base. The owner can change later through capture.

Each island has a shared daily dig limit

Farther islands: fewer digs, rarer treasure

Harbor Rush · The Mega Storm · 10

How a treasure find spreads. 1) A player docks and uses one of their 5 daily digs. 2) A big find pays that player a large reward. 3) The find is shared to faction chat and opens 50 smaller claims for other faction members, first come, first served, so whoever sails there fastest claims one; once all 50 are taken the treasure is gone. The grid shows 28 of 50 claims taken. Each island also has a shared daily dig limit, so crowds run it dry and players spread out. Farther islands allow fewer digs but hold rarer treasure. Digs refresh daily, every island is new after the storm, and successful digs score points for the faction.

The month · shops

Farther islands, better shops

Character copies

Rare upgrade resource

Late-game tech resource

Monthly cosmetic

Stronghold · a trickle

Far waters · plenty

Harbor Rush · The Mega Storm · 11

Every island has its own shop and quests, stocked by distance from safe water. Safe waters: one or two islands with very limited copies that rarely appear. Far waters: a large supply of character copies matching high-level upgrade needs, a rare resource needed for high-level characters, a late-game tech tree resource found only out there, and a monthly cosmetic to build toward.

The month · bosses

Krakens and Sea Dragons need everyone

Boss health · thousands of capped hits

24 h to kill

Rewards split by damage share

Red

Blue

Green

Yellow

Power = damage per hit

Idea: attack from anywhere

Harbor Rush · The Mega Storm · 12 · Shares shown are illustrative

Bosses have huge health pools. Each player can only hit a limited number of times; more account power means more damage per hit, but only mass participation brings one down. A boss escapes after 24 hours. In Uncharted Waters every faction can attack, and rewards split by each faction’s total damage. Open idea: once discovered, a boss could be attacked from anywhere without sailing. The biggest kaiju arrive in week 4.

Motivation

Explorers spread out. Warriors push out.

Explorers

Everywhere, mostly near home

Warriors

Packed into the contested middle

Your faction

Enemy faction

A faction needs both.

Harbor Rush · The Mega Storm · 13

Explorers (newer, weaker accounts) are scattered across the whole world but cluster around their own faction’s stronghold, charting, farming and digging in safer water. Warriors (stronger accounts) pack into the contested middle between factions, where PvP, the biggest bosses and enemy islands are. Shared dig limits push explorers apart; bosses and enemy islands pull warriors together. Neither type wins a month alone.

Harbor Rush · The Mega Storm · 14

Ship: a Fallout Shelter-style cutaway of the battleship where you drag characters into rooms and roles. When docked, characters split between ship and island. Island: third-person joystick exploration (a version is already built), with other players’ avatars running around like an MMO town; any character can be your avatar. Happiness rises from using a character’s card in battle and talking to them, never decays, and happy characters may gift resources. Only a few characters can be boosted per day, based on who randomly appears on the island.

Harbor Rush · The Mega Storm · 15 · Example roles. No role touches stamina, so map size stays calculable.

A Fallout Shelter-style cutaway of the battleship. Each room is a duty: Helm (Navigator, faster sailing), Crow’s Nest (Lookout, wider fog sight), Dig Locker (Digger, better treasure), Galley (Cook, happier crew), Gun Deck (Gunner, stronger combat), Armory (Bosun, tougher garrisons), plus Crew Quarters for resting and the Cargo Hold for storage. Dashed squares are open slots. Selecting a character opens their card: role, happiness, a line of dialogue, their role bonus, and actions to give a gift or reassign. Role names, numbers and the character are examples. No role touches stamina, so the stamina budget stays fixed and the map size stays calculable.

Harbor Rush · The Mega Storm · 16

One player’s daily loop. Collect the daily faction payout for islands owned. Sail out on stamina to chart new water or reach a target. Dock, use your 5 digs, and check the island’s shop and quests. Talk to the crew members you find on the island to boost happiness, and assign characters to ship roles. Spend your boss hits and attack enemy islands. Play core Harbor Rush hex matches, which use and level your character cards. Each of these actions earns faction score, covered on the next slide.

Harbor Rush · The Mega Storm · 17 · Split is illustrative; weights TBD

Most of a faction’s score is a wide spread of daily activity points, not just territory. Farther islands are worth more but are contested. Limits: 5 digs per player per day; farther islands allow fewer digs. Alliance and power balancing handles the rest of the anti-snowball work. The proportions in the bar are illustrative only.

The month · territory

Proposal · not locked

Garrisons slow the siege

Protected

Contested, week 2+

Light garrison: fewer wins to capture

Heavy garrison: many more wins

= one attacking win. Full bar = island changes hands.

Harbor Rush · The Mega Storm · 19

Faction members station characters on islands their faction owns. Every attacking win fills the siege meter; more defenders mean each win fills less, so even heavy attackers take time and many smaller wins still add up. Islands near strongholds are protected; Uncharted Waters are contested from week 2. Same-faction members can visit owned islands to shop and talk to NPCs; enemies can’t. Every faction member gets a daily payout per island owned. Placeholder to test, not locked.

Progression

Harbor Rush · The Mega Storm · 20

The personal tech tree has Attack, Defense and Exploration branches, is permanent for the account’s lifetime, scales hard at higher levels, and is upgraded with island resources. Strategy rotation lives in the cards, not the tech: each storm’s combat theme favors different cards, so players level different characters, which loops them back into the core hex battles.

Storm: final standings

Personal leaderboards · themed cosmetics

Harbor Rush · The Mega Storm · 21

Every day, each faction member is rewarded for the islands the faction owns. At the end of the month, rewards go out by faction standing, plus personal leaderboards for biggest score contribution, most boss damage, most islands discovered, most islands captured and most time sailed. Cosmetics follow each month’s theme. Several boards let every player type chase a title.

Red team

What players will say

“I don’t like my faction.”

Farm safe zones. Still rewarded.

“They beat me to my island.”

Healthy drama. Spread out next time. Beat enemies together.

“My friends ended up elsewhere.”

Alliances are blown together.

“Spenders grab everything.”

Speed-ups buy time, not number of captures.

“I joined mid-month.”

New water opens every day. Can still help Faction win.

Harbor Rush · The Mega Storm · 22

Faction: reroll early, don’t engage that month, or farm safe zones; participation and faction rewards still pay. Racing: healthy drama to a degree; spreading out is the smart play, and bosses and enemy islands give reasons to sail together. Friends: alliances of up to 30 always land in the same faction. Spenders: stamina is burned by distance, so speed-ups buy arrival time, not more map. Late joiners: the storm opens more water every day. The first two are the original red-team answers.

Harbor Rush · The Mega Storm · 23

Decided: replaces the Territory meta; 4 auto-assigned factions; alliances of up to 30; stamina burned by distance; target 2,500 per faction and 10,000 per world; no sharding in the MVP. Open: island combat format, week 3 content, garrison and siege model, boss attack range, stamina numbers and map size, faction reroll rules. Next mockups: globe in fog with strongholds, sailing and the Land ho! moment, island card (stamp, owner, shop, digs), ship cutaway with roles, boss damage board. Island counts and boss health should scale with world population so the design can be tested with a smaller soft-launch audience.
